name: Kalemegdan Fortress
description: Belgrade's historic citadel, set on the bluff where the Sava meets the Danube. Walk the ramparts, find the Victor monument, and watch sunset from the upper town.

name: Temple of Saint Sava
description: One of the largest Orthodox churches in the world. The interior mosaic, completed in 2020, is breathtaking — look up.

name: Skadarlija (Bohemian Quarter)
description: Cobblestoned, lantern-lit street of traditional kafanas. Live tamburica music most nights. Tourist-leaning but charming.

name: Beton Hala
description: Former concrete warehouse on the Sava waterfront, now a row of upmarket restaurants. Best for a long sunset dinner.

name: Splavovi (River Clubs)
description: Belgrade's legendary floating clubs along the Sava and Danube. Genres run from techno to turbofolk; pick your splav by the music.

name: Cetinjska Street
description: A ramshackle former brewery courtyard hosting a dozen bars. The local alternative-scene heart, busy from Thursday on.

name: Knez Mihailova
description: The pedestrian spine of the old town. Bookshops, ice cream, street performers, and grand 19th-century facades.

name: Trg Republike (Republic Square)
description: The city's central meeting point — "kod konja" (by the horse). Anchored by the National Museum and National Theatre.

name: National Museum of Serbia
description: Reopened in 2018 after a 15-year renovation. Strong on medieval Serbian art and a small but real Impressionist collection.

name: Nikola Tesla Museum
description: Compact museum in a 1920s villa with original Tesla devices and live coil demonstrations. Book ahead in summer.

name: House of Flowers (Tito's Mausoleum)
description: Tito's resting place inside the Museum of Yugoslavia complex. Pair with the main museum for a full Yugoslav-era afternoon.

name: Ada Ciganlija
description: Belgrade's "Sea" — a river island turned summer beach. Swimming, kayaking, beachside cafes, and 8 km of walking paths.

name: Zemun Quay & Gardoš Tower
description: Walk the Danube quay through old Zemun, then climb to Gardoš Tower for the postcard view back over the rooftops.

name: Gardoš (Millennium) Tower
description: Hilltop tower above Zemun built in 1896. Best sunset viewpoint in greater Belgrade.

name: Hotel Moskva (Café)
description: Art-Nouveau landmark from 1908. Order the Moskva Šnit cake with a coffee and watch all of Belgrade walk past.

name: Kafana ?
description: Belgrade's oldest kafana (1823), opposite the cathedral. The name is the literal punctuation — long story involving the church.

name: Smokvica
description: Hidden courtyard café with a fig tree at the centre. Brunch and shaded tables; arrive early on weekends.

name: Tašmajdan Park
description: Central park around Saint Mark's Church. Locals jog here; in summer, open-air concerts.

name: Saint Mark's Church
description: Serbo-Byzantine red-and-yellow brick church holding the tomb of Tsar Dušan. Quieter than Saint Sava, often overlooked.

name: Bajrakli Mosque
description: The only surviving Ottoman mosque in Belgrade, dating to the 1570s. Tucked into a narrow Dorćol street.

name: Residence of Princess Ljubica
description: 1830s Balkan-Ottoman townhouse, fully furnished. The smallest, most personal museum in town.

name: Belgrade Zoo (Vrt dobre nade)
description: Inside the Kalemegdan walls — strange and atmospheric, white tigers among the ramparts. Conditions are modest; bring perspective.

name: Ada Bridge
description: The 200-m pylon cable-stayed bridge that defines the modern skyline. Walk the pedestrian deck for river views.

name: Brankov Most
description: The walking deck across the Sava, between Old Belgrade and Novi Beograd. Best at blue hour.

name: Belgrade Waterfront Promenade
description: Polished new riverside promenade running south from Beton Hala. Controversial development, pleasant walk.

name: Savamala
description: Industrial-chic neighbourhood between the train tracks and the river. Galleries by day, bars by night.

name: Manak's House (Ethnographic)
description: Tiny Balkan-era house turned ethnographic museum. Costumes, textiles, and old Belgrade photographs.

name: Topčider Park
description: Royal-residence park with one of Europe's oldest plane trees (over 180 years). Picnic-perfect.

name: Avala Tower
description: 204-m TV tower on Avala mountain, 16 km out of town. Clear-day views to the Pannonian plain. Bus 401 from Voždovac.

name: Drugstore
description: Industrial techno club inside a former slaughterhouse. Friday/Saturday only, open late.

name: Magistrala
description: Specialty-coffee shop in Dorćol with consistent flat whites and an industrial fit-out. Take it to the river.

name: Supermarket Concept Store
description: Dorćol concept store with all-day brunch and a courtyard. Vegetarian-friendly, design-leaning crowd.
